response.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT p.birth_country, COUNT(*) AS tally FROM player_college pc JOIN player p ON p.player_id = pc.player_id GROUP BY p.birth_country), s AS (SELECT birth_country, tally, tally * 1.0 / SUM(tally) OVER () AS share, AVG(tally) OVER () AS avg_tally FROM t) SELECT SUM(tally) AS combined_tally, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(tally - avg_tally) AS avg_excess_over_avg_tally FROM s WHERE tally > avg_tally;

assumptions.assumption: Tally = number of player_college rows (player-college-year records) per birth_country, using an inner join to player so unmatched rows are dropped. Share = country tally / total tally over all countries. The average tally is the mean of the per-country tallies.
Players with a NULL birth_country form their own group and count as one 'country' in the total, the average and the share denominator.
player.player_id is unique, so the join does not duplicate rows.

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude players with a NULL birth_country, since NULL is not a real country. This changes the total, the average and the shares.
alternatives.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT p.birth_country, COUNT(*) AS tally FROM player_college pc JOIN player p ON p.player_id = pc.player_id WHERE p.birth_country IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.birth_country), s AS (SELECT birth_country, tally, tally * 1.0 / SUM(tally) OVER () AS share, AVG(tally) OVER () AS avg_tally FROM t) SELECT SUM(tally) AS combined_tally, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(tally - avg_tally) AS avg_excess_over_avg_tally FROM s WHERE tally > avg_tally;
